rationale: This MiBench security-sha target is tiny (1832 text bytes, 9 functions) with one dominant hot function, sha_transform (667 bytes, the SHA round loop), so passes whose overhead scales with executed blocks or basic-block count must be gated by high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights: FLA and BCF get strong SecurityGain (0.85/0.80) because flattening and bogus-control-flow most disrupt static analysis of the round function, but their RuntimeCost (0.85) and SizeCost (0.80-0.85) weights ensure they are only applied where features justify it, protecting the hot loop and the small binary's code-size budget. SUB is favored broadly (SecurityGain 0.70, low risk/cost) as a cheap baseline transformation over the arithmetic-heavy SHA constants. SPLIT and IBR get moderate weights as low-to-medium overhead structural diversifiers useful on a program this small, while IGV is weighted cheap on runtime and size (0.20) since global-buffer indirection suits sha_stream's state arrays. ICALL is weakest (SecurityGain 0.40, CorrectnessRisk 0.40) because the program has few indirect-call opportunities and dispatch-through-pointer conversion on a hot cryptographic loop risks both performance and correctness; CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low (0.20-0.40) everywhere since SHA's bit-manipulation is easy to verify but the driver's I/O path tolerates little transformation error.
